title: Add a read-only OAuth mode for safe autonomous tool use
body:
### Motivation

- Add an OAuth flow option for read-only integration so users can authenticate with a least-privilege token. 
- Prevent accidental data mutation when the CLI is authenticated with a read-only OAuth token. 

### Description

- Introduces read-only OAuth support by adding a `--read-only` option to `td auth login`, extending `buildAuthorizationUrl` to accept a `readOnly` option, and saving auth metadata (`auth_mode` and `auth_scope`) alongside tokens in the config. 
- Treats externally provided tokens (environment variable or manual `td auth token`) as `unknown` mode and persists `auth_mode: 'unknown'` when saving manual tokens. 
- Adds a `permissions` module that identifies mutating API calls and sync payloads and exposes `ensureWriteAllowed` which throws when the stored auth mode is `read-only`. 
- Wraps the Todoist API client in `createSpinnerWrappedApi` to run `ensureWriteAllowed` before mutating calls, preserve spinner/progress behavior, and emit progress events and errors consistently. 
- Updates CLI docs and help content (`README.md` and skill content) to document the read-only login flow and auth metadata behavior. 
- Updates and adds unit tests to cover the new behavior and metadata handling. 

### Testing

- Ran unit tests with `vitest` including modified `src/__tests__/auth.test.ts` and new tests `src/__tests__/oauth.test.ts` and `src/__tests__/permissions.test.ts`, and all tests passed. 
- Verified the OAuth authorization URL uses `data:read` when `--read-only` is passed via the new `buildAuthorizationUrl` unit test. 
- Verified that write operations are blocked when `getAuthMetadata` reports `authMode: 'read-only'` via the `permissions` unit tests.

title: feat: add --stdin flag to comment add, task add, and task update
body:
Closes #86

## Summary

- Adds `--stdin` flag to `td comment add` to pipe comment content from stdin, avoiding shell escaping issues with multiline content
- Extends the same `--stdin` pattern to `td task add` and `td task update` for piping task descriptions

Errors clearly when both the inline flag (`--content` / `--description`) and `--stdin` are provided simultaneously.

## Usage

```bash
# Comment add (original issue)
cat note.md | td comment add id:6g3CVXCP4XQ8XWGW --stdin
td comment add "task name" --stdin < note.md

# Task add/update (extended)
td task add "My task" --stdin < description.md
cat notes.md | td task add "My task" --stdin
td task update "task name" --stdin < description.md
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm test -- comment` — existing stdin tests for comment add
- [ ] `npm test -- task` — 6 new tests covering stdin read, conflict error, and multiline content for both `task add` and `task update`

title: feat: add task reschedule command
body:
## Summary
- Adds `td task reschedule [ref] [date]` command that uses the Sync API to move task due dates while **preserving recurrence patterns**, timezone, and time-of-day
- Unlike `task update --due` (which uses REST API and replaces the entire due string), reschedule only updates `due.date` — keeping `isRecurring`, `string`, `timezone`, and `lang` intact
- Accepts ISO format dates (`YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`); preserves existing time when only a date is provided

Similar to https://github.com/Doist/todoist-ai/pull/382

## Test plan
